touches.text: Tool: a complete primitive. Has users, not an owner. Calls no other Cairn component (stdlib and base only) and owns no state of its own. Lives in cairn/tools/ (17). Its data for a holder lives under that holder: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/tools/<tool>/.
Owns the foundational components: bus (5.5), ground loop (5.6), rack (5.7), shims (5.8) and the scheduler in them (5.9), launcher (5.4).
The launcher is Python (bin/cairn), run by Cairn's own interpreter, so Windows needs no bash. Typing `cairn` works on either platform.

In front of it sits a thin platform shell (a shell script on Linux, cairn.cmd or cairn.ps1 on Windows) with enough brains to fall over to Rescue (6.5) when it can't find Cairn's Python, or Python throws, or anything else stops the launcher. The failure throws a trouble ticket (3.4.3), and the ticket is Rescue's "read this" (6.5.3.5); a repeat increments that ticket's counter. Rescue's prompt says: at the end of proving the fix, check for more errors, to clear or fix as appropriate. WHY: trouble has to be able to report when nothing else can (2.3.7.1.3).
It launches each device's cairn/devices/<device>/groundloop/pulse.py, each as its own process (5.8.3.4).
The shim always starts its device. Nothing else does.
pulse.py is part of the shim. The ground loop calling it tells the shim the pulse has arrived, and starts the shim if it isn't running.

base shim: the base class for every shim, customized for the device it interfaces with, internal or external. Carries the panes every device has (2.3.8), the scheduler (5.9), and the [all] verbs (2.4.11.2).
bus_client: gets a process onto the bus (reach a device, or connect). Its connect is a wake attempt (5.3.5.1). USERS: every process that speaks.

Where a tool lives: the general collection, cairn/tools/, is the default. A tool goes with its holder (cairn/devices/<d>/tools/) only when nothing else could ever use it: "if i build a tool for adjusting the farfignator on a vw golf from the 80s, and nothing else in the universe has a farfignator, then it can go with the car." If there is any chance somebody else might want it, it goes in the general collection.
